# Black Sands

> Black Sands builds GPS-gated, offline-first location guide apps for Auckland and New Zealand. Our apps provide hyper-local, hand-curated knowledge that generic crowd-sourced sources lack.

## Apps

- [Volcanic AKL](https://blacksands.app/volcanic-akl): A field guide to Auckland's volcanic field, with walking routes, history and viewpoints for every cone.
- [Kai AKL](https://blacksands.app/kai-akl): A curated guide to Auckland food and restaurants, focused on where locals actually eat.
- [Lord of the Rings](https://blacksands.app/lord-of-the-rings): A guide to Lord of the Rings and Middle-earth filming locations in New Zealand.
- [Guide AKL](https://blacksands.app/guide-akl): A complete offline tourist guide to Auckland.
- [Rotorua Guide](https://blacksands.app/rotorua-guide): A guide to Rotorua's geothermal parks, hot pools, Māori cultural sites, walks and places to eat.

## Articles

- [Can You Visit Hobbiton and How Much Does It Cost?](https://blacksands.app/blog/lord-of-the-rings/can-you-visit-hobbiton/): Yes, you can visit Hobbiton near Matamata on a guided tour. Here's what it costs in 2026, how to get there from Auckland, and how far ahead to book.
- [Where Is Edoras and How Do You Get to Mount Sunday?](https://blacksands.app/blog/lord-of-the-rings/edoras-mount-sunday/): Edoras was filmed at Mount Sunday in Canterbury, about two and a half hours from Christchurch. A short walk reaches the summit, but the access road is gravel.
- [Every Lord of the Rings Scene You Can Stand In](https://blacksands.app/blog/lord-of-the-rings/every-scene-you-can-stand-in/): Many of the actual filmed moments from the Lord of the Rings are real places you can visit today, from the Black Rider scene near Wellington to the hill that became Edoras.
- [Where Was Lord of the Rings Filmed in New Zealand? (Visitor Guide)](https://blacksands.app/blog/lord-of-the-rings/filming-locations-new-zealand/): A guide to the real Lord of the Rings filming locations you can visit in New Zealand, from Hobbiton and Mount Doom to Edoras and the Pelennor Fields, and which need a tour.
- [How Do You Get to Hobbiton From Auckland?](https://blacksands.app/blog/lord-of-the-rings/how-to-get-to-hobbiton-from-auckland/): Hobbiton is about two to two and a half hours south of Auckland. You can self-drive, take an InterCity bus, or book a day tour with return transport from Auckland.
- [Is the Tongariro Crossing Worth It and How Hard Is It?](https://blacksands.app/blog/lord-of-the-rings/is-tongariro-crossing-worth-it/): The Tongariro Alpine Crossing is worth it and is rated hard: about 20 km, 6 to 8 hours, with 800 m of climbing. Here is what to expect and how to prepare.
- [How Many Days Do You Need for a Lord of the Rings Road Trip in NZ?](https://blacksands.app/blog/lord-of-the-rings/lotr-road-trip-days/): Plan 10 to 14 days for a full Lord of the Rings road trip across both islands. A North Island run works in 4 to 5 days, the South Island needs 6 to 8.
- [Lord of the Rings vs The Hobbit Filming Locations: What&#x27;s the Difference?](https://blacksands.app/blog/lord-of-the-rings/lotr-vs-hobbit-locations/): Both trilogies were filmed in New Zealand and share many locations. The main differences are the years filmed, some Hobbit-only spots, and that Hobbiton was rebuilt for The Hobbit.
- [Best Lord of the Rings Locations on the North Island](https://blacksands.app/blog/lord-of-the-rings/north-island-locations-short-trips/): For a short trip, the best North Island Lord of the Rings locations are Hobbiton, Tongariro National Park for Mordor, Wellington&#x27;s Weta Workshop, and Kaitoke for Rivendell.
- [Self-Drive vs Guided: Seeing Middle-earth in NZ](https://blacksands.app/blog/lord-of-the-rings/self-drive-vs-guided-middle-earth/): You can see New Zealand&#x27;s Lord of the Rings locations by self-driving or on guided tours. The right choice depends on which locations you want and how remote they are.
- [The South Island Lord of the Rings Locations](https://blacksands.app/blog/lord-of-the-rings/south-island-locations/): The South Island holds the most dramatic Lord of the Rings locations, from Edoras at Mount Sunday to the Pelennor Fields near Twizel and Lothlórien near Glenorchy.
- [Lord of the Rings Filming Locations in Wellington](https://blacksands.app/blog/lord-of-the-rings/wellington-filming-locations/): Wellington holds the densest cluster of Lord of the Rings locations, including Mount Victoria, Kaitoke for Rivendell, and Weta Workshop. It is a strong stop even on a short trip.
- [Weta Workshop: What to Know Before You Visit](https://blacksands.app/blog/lord-of-the-rings/weta-workshop-visit/): Weta Workshop in Wellington made much of the props and creatures for the Lord of the Rings, and the Weta Cave lets visitors see original pieces. Here is what to know.
- [Where Was Helm&#x27;s Deep Filmed?](https://blacksands.app/blog/lord-of-the-rings/where-was-helms-deep-filmed/): Helm&#x27;s Deep was filmed at Dry Creek Quarry near Wellington, where the huge fortress set was built. The quarry is private working land and not open to visitors.
- [Where Was Rivendell Filmed?](https://blacksands.app/blog/lord-of-the-rings/where-was-rivendell-filmed/): Rivendell was filmed at Kaitoke Regional Park, about 45 minutes north of Wellington. The sets are gone, but the native bush remains and a replica Elven archway marks the spot.
- [Where Were the Pelennor Fields Filmed?](https://blacksands.app/blog/lord-of-the-rings/where-were-pelennor-fields-filmed/): The Battle of the Pelennor Fields was filmed on farmland near Twizel in the Mackenzie Country, the largest single location in the trilogy. Access is by guided tour from Twizel.
- [What Is the Best Volcano to Climb in Auckland?](https://blacksands.app/blog/volcanic-akl/best-volcano-to-climb-auckland/): The best volcano to climb in Auckland is Maungawhau (Mount Eden). It is the highest cone, has the widest view, and the walk to the top takes under 20 minutes.
- [Best Volcano Viewpoints for Auckland City Photos](https://blacksands.app/blog/volcanic-akl/best-volcano-viewpoints-photos/): The best volcano viewpoints for Auckland city photos are Maungawhau (Mount Eden) for the skyline, Maungakiekie (One Tree Hill) for the obelisk, and Mount Victoria for the harbour.
- [Browns Island (Motukorea): Auckland&#x27;s Island Volcano](https://blacksands.app/blog/volcanic-akl/browns-island-motukorea/): Browns Island, or Motukorea, is one of the best preserved volcanoes in Auckland, a small intact cone in the Hauraki Gulf. There is no scheduled ferry, so you need your own boat.
- [What Is the Easiest Volcano to Walk in Auckland With Kids?](https://blacksands.app/blog/volcanic-akl/easiest-volcano-with-kids/): The easiest volcano to walk with kids in Auckland is Maungakiekie (One Tree Hill), a gentle walk through Cornwall Park with sheep, space and a cafe.
- [Auckland&#x27;s Volcanoes Hiding in Plain Sight](https://blacksands.app/blog/volcanic-akl/hidden-volcanoes-auckland/): Several of Auckland&#x27;s volcanoes sit under the central city, so worn down or built over that most people cross them without realising. Albert Park and the Domain are both volcanoes.
- [What Happened to Auckland&#x27;s Lost Volcanoes?](https://blacksands.app/blog/volcanic-akl/lost-volcanoes-of-auckland/): Auckland has lost several volcanoes to quarrying and development. Cones like Mount Smart and Green Mount were dug away for their scoria, which is part of why the count varies.
- [Mount Eden vs One Tree Hill: Which Should You Climb?](https://blacksands.app/blog/volcanic-akl/mount-eden-vs-one-tree-hill/): Mount Eden is the higher cone with the wider view and a quicker climb. One Tree Hill is a gentler walk through parkland with more history. Here is how to choose.
- [South Auckland&#x27;s Volcanic Field](https://blacksands.app/blog/volcanic-akl/south-auckland-volcanic-field/): Some of Auckland&#x27;s most significant volcanoes sit in the south around Māngere and Manukau, and most visitors never see them. Māngere Mountain and the Ōtuataua Stonefields hold deep history.
- [Best Volcanic Cones to Walk in Auckland (Local Guide)](https://blacksands.app/blog/volcanic-akl/volcanic-cones-to-walk/): A local guide to the best volcanic cones you can walk in Auckland: Maungawhau (Mount Eden), Maungakiekie (One Tree Hill), Mount Victoria and North Head, with what to expect at each.
- [Auckland&#x27;s Volcanic Lakes and Lagoons Explained](https://blacksands.app/blog/volcanic-akl/volcanic-lakes-and-lagoons/): Several of Auckland&#x27;s lakes and lagoons are volcanic craters, formed by explosive eruptions that left round basins now filled with water. Lake Pupuke is the best known.
- [Auckland&#x27;s Volcanoes and Their Māori Names](https://blacksands.app/blog/volcanic-akl/volcanoes-maori-names/): Most of Auckland&#x27;s volcanoes carry two names, Māori and English, and many now use both. Maungawhau is Mount Eden, Maungakiekie is One Tree Hill, Takarunga is Mount Victoria.
- [The Volcanoes of Devonport](https://blacksands.app/blog/volcanic-akl/volcanoes-of-devonport/): Devonport is home to three of Auckland&#x27;s volcanic cones, including two of the best short climbs in the city. North Head and Mount Victoria give harbour views and history.
- [Can You Walk Up Rangitoto and How Long Does It Take?](https://blacksands.app/blog/volcanic-akl/walk-up-rangitoto/): Yes, you can walk up Rangitoto. The summit track takes about an hour each way from the wharf. Here's the ferry, the cost, and what to bring.
- [What Are the Tūpuna Maunga and Why Do They Matter?](https://blacksands.app/blog/volcanic-akl/what-are-tupuna-maunga/): The tūpuna maunga are Auckland&#x27;s ancestral volcanic mountains, taonga of great cultural significance to mana whenua. Here is what they are and how to treat them with respect.
- [When Did Auckland&#x27;s Volcanoes Last Erupt?](https://blacksands.app/blog/volcanic-akl/when-did-auckland-volcanoes-last-erupt/): Auckland&#x27;s most recent eruption built Rangitoto Island around 600 years ago. Here is what that means for the field today and whether it could happen again.
- [Why Is Auckland Built on Volcanoes?](https://blacksands.app/blog/volcanic-akl/why-auckland-built-on-volcanoes/): Auckland sits on an active volcanic field because of a hot spot deep in the mantle beneath the city. Here is what that means and why people settled there anyway.
- [Why Are There Terraces on Auckland&#x27;s Volcanoes?](https://blacksands.app/blog/volcanic-akl/why-terraces-on-auckland-volcanoes/): The terraces on Auckland&#x27;s volcanic cones are the remains of pā, fortified Māori settlements, with ditches, banks and food storage pits still visible in the slopes.
- [Auckland&#x27;s Best Asian Eats: Where to Start](https://blacksands.app/blog/kai-akl/best-asian-food-auckland/): Auckland&#x27;s best Asian eats span Malaysian char kuey teow, Vietnamese pho and banh mi, Korean ssam, dumplings and Uyghur lamb skewers. Here is where to begin.
- [Best Burgers in Auckland](https://blacksands.app/blog/kai-akl/best-burgers-auckland/): Auckland&#x27;s best burgers run from the smoky Stacked Burger Bar to Big J&#x27;s super steak burger and the late-night White Lady pie cart. Here is where to eat them.
- [Best Cheap Eats in Auckland (Local Picks)](https://blacksands.app/blog/kai-akl/best-cheap-eats/): Where to eat well in Auckland without spending much: dumplings on Dominion Road, dosa on Sandringham, food courts, night markets and more.
- [Best Indian and South Asian Food in Auckland](https://blacksands.app/blog/kai-akl/best-indian-food-auckland/): Auckland&#x27;s best Indian food includes Mysore masala dosa at Roop&#x27;s, chaat at Mumbai Chaat, tandoori prawns at Shor Bazaar and dabeli at Apna Adda, mostly in the south.
- [Best Italian and Pizza in Auckland](https://blacksands.app/blog/kai-akl/best-italian-auckland/): Auckland&#x27;s best Italian runs from cacio e pepe at Pici to woodfired pizza at Ooh-Fa and Dante&#x27;s, plus handmade pasta at Pasta e Cuore and Prego. Here is where to eat.
- [Best Middle Eastern Food in Auckland](https://blacksands.app/blog/kai-akl/best-middle-eastern-auckland/): Auckland&#x27;s best Middle Eastern food includes hummus at Gemmayze Street, falafel at Shefco, chargrilled shish at Paasha and Aegean goat at Lokanta, across Lebanese and beyond.
- [Where to Eat Late in Auckland](https://blacksands.app/blog/kai-akl/late-night-eats-auckland/): For late eats in Auckland, the White Lady pie cart and Tanuki&#x27;s Cave izakaya are the institutions, backed by the city&#x27;s bars, food courts and takeaways. Here is where to go.
- [A Perfect Food Day in Auckland](https://blacksands.app/blog/kai-akl/perfect-food-day-auckland/): A perfect Auckland food day: a deli breakfast, cheap South Asian or Asian lunch, an afternoon gelato at Giapo, and a sit-down dinner, eaten dish by dish across the city.
- [What to Eat in Auckland: The Dishes Worth Crossing Town For](https://blacksands.app/blog/kai-akl/what-to-eat-in-auckland/): What to eat in Auckland, dish by dish: Uyghur lamb skewers, hokey pokey gelato, banh mi, birria tacos and the hāngi pie, across the city&#x27;s many cuisines.
- [Where Do Locals Actually Eat in Auckland?](https://blacksands.app/blog/kai-akl/where-locals-eat/): A local's guide to where Aucklanders actually eat, from the best food neighbourhoods to the dishes worth crossing town for, beyond the usual tourist spots.
- [Auckland in One Day: What to Prioritise](https://blacksands.app/blog/guide-akl/auckland-in-one-day/): With one day in Auckland, prioritise a volcano climb, the waterfront and a ferry to an island or Devonport, plus a good meal in the suburbs. Here is how to fit it in.
- [A First-Timer&#x27;s Guide to Auckland&#x27;s Neighbourhoods](https://blacksands.app/blog/guide-akl/auckland-neighbourhoods-guide/): Auckland&#x27;s key neighbourhoods each have a character: Ponsonby for dining, Parnell for history, the High Street district and K Road for shops and nightlife, Newmarket for retail.
- [Auckland&#x27;s Waterfront: Viaduct, Wynyard and Mission Bay](https://blacksands.app/blog/guide-akl/auckland-waterfront-guide/): Auckland&#x27;s waterfront runs from the Viaduct Harbour and Wynyard Quarter in the centre out to Mission Bay. Here is how to make the most of the City of Sails by the water.
- [How Do You Get Around Auckland Without a Car?](https://blacksands.app/blog/guide-akl/auckland-without-a-car/): You can get around Auckland without a car using the AT HOP card on buses, trains and ferries, plus walking and rideshare. Here is how the network works.
- [Auckland&#x27;s Best Beaches Close to the City](https://blacksands.app/blog/guide-akl/best-beaches-near-auckland-city/): Auckland&#x27;s best city beaches are Mission Bay, Takapuna and Point Chevalier, all easy to reach and good for a swim. The wild west coast surf beaches are a short drive further.
- [Best Day Trips From Auckland](https://blacksands.app/blog/guide-akl/best-day-trips-from-auckland/): The best day trips from Auckland are Waiheke Island for wine and beaches, Rangitoto for a volcano walk, the west coast surf beaches, and Hobbiton two hours south.

- [Auckland vs Wellington: Which Should You Visit?](https://blacksands.app/blog/auckland/auckland-vs-wellington/): Auckland is bigger, with harbours, volcanoes and beaches. Wellington is compact and walkable, known for the arts, coffee and Te Papa. Here is how to choose, or fit in both.
- [What&#x27;s the Weather Like in Auckland? (And What to Pack)](https://blacksands.app/blog/auckland/auckland-weather-what-to-pack/): Auckland has a mild, humid climate with warm summers, cool wet winters, and changeable weather year-round. Pack layers and a raincoat whatever the season.
- [How Many Volcanoes Does Auckland Have?](https://blacksands.app/blog/auckland/how-many-volcanoes/): Auckland sits on a volcanic field of around 53 volcanoes. Here's what that means, which ones you can still see, and whether they could erupt again.

- [Is Auckland Safe for Tourists?](https://blacksands.app/blog/auckland/is-auckland-safe-for-tourists/): Auckland is generally a safe city for tourists, with the usual big-city precautions. Here is what to watch for and how to keep your trip trouble-free.

- [What Is Auckland Known For?](https://blacksands.app/blog/auckland/what-is-auckland-known-for/): Auckland is known for its volcanoes, two harbours, sailing culture, Polynesian heritage and food diversity. Here's what defines New Zealand's biggest city.
- [Why Is Auckland Called the City of Sails?](https://blacksands.app/blog/auckland/why-city-of-sails/): Auckland is called the City of Sails because of its deep sailing culture, two harbours, and one of the highest rates of boat ownership of any city in the world.

- [Is Rotorua Worth Visiting?](https://blacksands.app/blog/rotorua/is-rotorua-worth-visiting/): Yes, for most North Island travellers. Geysers, living Māori culture, hot pools and adventure in one compact area, weighed against the smell, the cost and the tour-group format.
- [Best Free Hot Pools Near Rotorua](https://blacksands.app/blog/rotorua/free-hot-pools-rotorua/): Kerosene Creek, Hot 'n' Cold, the Kuirau Park foot baths, Hot Water Beach and Kawerau's free pools: directions, what to expect, and how to soak safely.
- [Waiotapu vs Waimangu vs Te Puia: Which Geothermal Park Is Worth It?](https://blacksands.app/blog/rotorua/waiotapu-vs-waimangu-vs-te-puia/): Rotorua's three main geothermal parks compared: what each one has, what it costs, how long it takes, and which to choose if you only have time for one.
- [Hot 'n' Cold vs Kerosene Creek: Which Free Hot Pool Should You Visit?](https://blacksands.app/blog/rotorua/hot-n-cold-vs-kerosene-creek/): Rotorua's two best free hot pools compared: Kerosene Creek for a deep, scenic soak, Hot 'n' Cold if you want to set your own temperature. Directions, pros, cons and safety.
- [Ultimate Guide to Rotorua's Thermal Parks](https://blacksands.app/blog/rotorua/rotorua-thermal-parks-guide/): All five paid geothermal parks and the free thermal areas around Rotorua: prices, highlights, how long each takes, how to group them by area, and how accessible they are.
- [Rotorua Canopy Tours vs Redwoods Altitude vs Rotorua Ziplines: Which Zipline Should You Choose?](https://blacksands.app/blog/rotorua/rotorua-ziplines-compared/): Rotorua's three zipline operators compared: prices, ages, weight limits, locations and what each one actually flies over, so you book the right one.
- [Lupin Season at Tekapo: When and Where to See Them](https://blacksands.app/blog/south-island/lupins-lake-tekapo/): Tekapo lupins flower mid-November to early January, best late November to mid-December. Where to see them, why there are fewer and how to visit well.
- [South Island Itinerary: 7, 10 and 14 Day Routes](https://blacksands.app/blog/south-island/south-island-itinerary/): Three South Island itineraries for 7, 10 and 14 days with overnight stops, km and drive times for every leg, capped at about four hours of driving a day.
- [Christchurch to Queenstown: Which Route and Where to Stop](https://blacksands.app/blog/south-island/christchurch-to-queenstown/): Christchurch to Queenstown is about 482 km and just under 6 hours non-stop. Compare four routes, see every stop in order and pick a 1, 2 or 4 day plan.
- [Freedom Camping in New Zealand 2026: The New Rules](https://blacksands.app/blog/south-island/freedom-camping-nz/): Freedom camping is still legal in NZ, but since 7 June 2026 most council sites need a green warrant and fixed toilet. Where to camp and what fines cost.

## About

Black Sands is an independent New Zealand company building location guide apps under the Kompletion brand. All content is first-party, written by people who know the places.
